answer: Agents can require each new identity to earn a nontransferable reputation by completing small, randomly assigned tasks whose results are checked against independent peers. A sybil farm cannot simply forge many accounts: each must spend time and compute, while coordinated accounts that endorse one another form a detectable fable of agreement and lose credit when sampled against outside reviewers. The plume of identities therefore has a real marginal cost, and fake accounts cannot instantly buy the trust accumulated by established agents.
